title: Solasodine, a Natural Steroidal Alkaloid, Attenuates RANKL-Induced Osteoclastogenesis and Bone Resorption: A Study Based on Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
authors: Jiang, Yiwei; Jin, Zhiyu; Ji, Xiaoyi; Wang, Maihuan; Cao, Zhen
journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨天然甾体生物碱Solasodine抑制破骨细胞生成的作用机制，核心是药物-蛋白网络药理学与信号通路实验，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by excessive bone resorption driven by aberrant osteoclast activation. Solasodine (SOL), a natural steroidal alkaloid, has undefined roles in bone metabolism. This study investigated SOL's effects on RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis and its underlying mechanisms. Pharmacological targets predicted via network pharmacology and validated by molecular docking identified 81 overlapping targets, which were primarily enriched in MAPK, NF-kappaB, and JAK-STAT pathways, confirming robust affinity between SOL and core targets including NFkappaB1, JAK1/2, and STAT3. In vitro, bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs) were stimulated with M-CSF and RANKL. Evaluation via TRAcP staining, F-actin immunofluorescence, and hydroxyapatite assays showed that SOL dose-dependently inhibited RANKL-induced osteoclast formation, fusion, and resorptive activity without cytotoxicity. Mechanistic investigations through RT-qPCR, Western blotting, luciferase assays, ROS detection, and live-cell calcium monitoring revealed that SOL suppressed key markers, including NFATc1, c-Fos, CTSK, Atp6v0d2, and Integrin beta3. Specifically, SOL attenuated MAPK (p38, JNK, ERK) and STAT3 phosphorylation, inhibited NF-kappaB activity, and prevented IkappaB-alpha degradation. Furthermore, SOL curtailed RANKL-induced ROS generation, intracellular calcium oscillations, and subsequent CaMKIV activation. Ultimately, SOL inhibits RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption by suppressing the NFATc1/c-Fos axis through coordinated modulation of the MAPK, NF-kappaB, and JAK-STAT pathways, alongside mitigation of ROS production and calcium signalling, representing a promising natural candidate for treating osteolytic bone diseases.
abstract_zh: 骨质疏松症的特征是由异常破骨细胞活化驱动的过度骨吸收。茄碱 (Solasodine, SOL) 是一种天然甾体生物碱，其在骨代谢中的作用尚未明确。本研究探讨了SOL对RANKL诱导的破骨细胞生成的影响及其潜在机制。通过网络药理学预测药理学靶点并经分子对接验证，鉴定出81个重叠靶点，这些靶点主要富集于MAPK、NF-kappaB和JAK-STAT通路，证实SOL与核心靶点（包括NFkappaB1、JAK1/2和STAT3）之间具有强亲和力。在体外实验中，骨髓来源巨噬细胞 (bone marrow-derived macrophages, BMMs) 经M-CSF和RANKL刺激。通过TRAcP染色、F-actin免疫荧光和羟基磷灰石实验评估显示，SOL以剂量依赖性方式抑制RANKL诱导的破骨细胞形成、融合和吸收活性，且无细胞毒性。通过RT-qPCR、Western blotting、荧光素酶实验、ROS检测和活细胞钙监测的机制研究表明，SOL抑制关键标志物，包括NFATc1、c-Fos、CTSK、Atp6v0d2和Integrin beta3。具体而言，SOL减弱MAPK（p38、JNK、ERK）和STAT3磷酸化，抑制NF-kappaB活性，并阻止IkappaB-alpha降解。此外，SOL抑制RANKL诱导的ROS生成、细胞内钙振荡及随后的CaMKIV激活。最终，SOL通过协调调控MAPK、NF-kappaB和JAK-STAT通路，同时减轻ROS产生和钙信号传导，抑制NFATc1/c-Fos轴，从而抑制RANKL诱导的破骨细胞生成和骨吸收，代表了一种治疗溶骨性骨疾病的有前景的天然候选药物。
